prediction.text:
In its fiscal 2025 10-K risk factors, NVIDIA said U.S. export controls on China are a material and changing risk. It said the U.S. government has changed the rules and may change them again at any time. It said this could effectively exclude NVIDIA from all or part of the China market and push Chinese customers toward alternatives. NVIDIA also said the possibility of further controls has hurt demand and could disrupt its supply chain. It also said violations could bring penalties.
NVIDIA described the existing restrictions: in the third quarter of fiscal 2023 the U.S. government announced export restrictions and licensing requirements targeting China's semiconductor and supercomputing industries. In October 2023 it announced new and updated licensing requirements, effective in NVIDIA's fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, for exports to China and Country Groups D1, D4, and D5.
NVIDIA warned that the USG has changed and may again change the export control rules at any time. It said this could subject a wider range of its products to export restrictions and licensing requirements, negatively impacting its business and financial results.
NVIDIA said the controls could effectively exclude it from all or part of the China market, as well as other impacted markets, including the Middle East and countries designated "Tier 2" by the AI Diffusion IFR. It also said they could encourage customers in China to pursue alternatives, including suppliers based in China, Europe, and Israel.
NVIDIA said export controls could disrupt its supply chain and distribution channels, hurting its ability to serve demand, including in markets outside China and for its gaming products. It said the possibility of additional controls has negatively impacted, and may in the future negatively impact, demand for its products, benefiting competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted.
NVIDIA noted that violating U.S. or similar non-U.S. export control or sanctions laws, even without its knowledge, could lead to various penalties. It also said the focus on AI's strategic importance has produced regulatory restrictions on AI-enabling products and may bring additional restrictions affecting some or all of its offerings.

caveats: The evidence covers four Item 1A passages from the FY2025 10-K. Two other relevant passages, on customers outside China designing out U.S. semiconductors and on additional unilateral or multilateral controls and foreign government responses, could not be read in full and are not quoted.
The passages describe the risk qualitatively and do not quantify any revenue impact.
